scenes.text: People notice you far less than you think they do.
Psychologists call it the spotlight effect.
In a Cornell study, students had to walk into a room wearing an embarrassing Barry Manilow T-shirt.
They guessed about half the people in the room would notice it.
In reality, only about a quarter did.
So that awkward moment you keep replaying? Most people already forgot it.
What's something you were sure everyone noticed?

title: Nobody is watching you as much as you think 👀
caption: The spotlight effect: in a 2000 Cornell study (Gilovich et al.), students wearing an embarrassing T-shirt thought about half the room noticed. Only about a quarter actually did. 👀
